Here the Persian glossator wanders far from the point; see our Prolegomena II, p. 91. One cannot, as he does, identify this lamp with the Active Intelligence—for the simple reason that this is the very Intelligence the pilgrim will later rejoin at the mystical Sinai. The act of “setting down this lamp” would make no sense on the glossator’s reading. Moreover, he seems completely to forget that the hierarchy of the Angeli intellectuales is situated in Nâ-kojâ-Abâd, beyond Mount Qâf—that is, beyond the system of the Spheres. As for the waterwheel mentioned in stanza 33, it denotes the Moon’s sphere; but the mystic himself is a moon “in the heaven of tawhîd” (the affirmation of divine oneness). She enters that spiritual form, shapes and orders it within the New Man, so that it bears the seal and imprint of the limbs of the Maiden of Light who dwells in him. She is “the one called the hour of life, which is the first.
